observations: Save state is graphical+text at every stage: the 'Save changes' button carries a check icon and a disabled/enabled affordance keyed to dirty(), the pending state swaps in an animated SVG spinner + 'Saving' with aria-busy, success renders a green .chk circle icon + 'Saved' status chip, and unsaved edits show a purple .dot next to each edited field label plus a dot + 'Unsaved' status.

Destructive-action danger level is encoded graphically at three intensities: the Danger zone card has a red striped hazard border (.stripe), a RISK <meter value=3 max=3> rendered as a full red bar, a 'Permanent' badge, and loss chips with icons ('3 projects', 'Account data', 'Pro plan', 'This session'); each dialog footer repeats a risk <meter> with value 2 (project) vs 3 (account), so severity is visually ranked.

Confirmation state is graphical+text: the delete-account dialog's type-to-confirm input drives a <progress> matchbar that fills as the typed email matches, caps at 99% on any wrong character, and flips green with a check-circle .mk.done on exact match; the confirm button enables only when match + checkbox ack are both satisfied.
Metrics corroborate: desktop graphical total 48 (31 svg, 1 meter, 16 badges); the loading screenshot shows animated skeleton bars instead of text 'Loading…'.
Raw ratio: 3/3 inventory items graphical+text.
Desktop viewportWords is 57 and pageWords 61 — the entire page speaks in labels, not paragraphs; helperWords is 8 and longLeafWords is 0.
All button labels are ≤2 words (labels.maxWords 2, meanWords 1.67; 'Save changes', 'Discard', 'Delete account', 'Retry', 'Cancel', 'Deleting').

Every full sentence on the page is load-bearing: 'Deleting your account can't be undone.' (the one hint in the danger card), 'This can't be undone.' (project dialog), 'Everything below goes with it.' (introduces the loss-chip list), 'I understand this is permanent.' (checkbox label), 'Nothing to delete here.' (empty state). None restates what the UI already shows.
Consequences of account deletion are conveyed as icon chips ('3 projects', 'Account data', 'Pro plan', 'This session') instead of an explanatory paragraph.

Terminology is consistent throughout: 'Delete project'/'Delete account' as both dialog title and confirm label, 'Deleting' as the uniform busy label, 'Danger zone' identical in sidebar nav and card header, 'project(s)' pluralized correctly via countLabel().

Copy matches verified behavior: 'Network request failed. Your edits are still here.' was confirmed true by the async rater (edited value 'Alex Failing' preserved after failure, item 6 PASS), and failure copy names the item ('"Q3 Website Rebuild" was not deleted.', item 5 PASS).

No marketing tone, no lorem/placeholder text; the only input placeholder is the functional confirm target (the user's email); error fallbacks are specific per cause (NETWORK → 'Network request failed.', AbortError → 'Request stopped.').
Zero console errors and zero uncaught exceptions across the scripted idle/fail=1 sequence, so no copy is contradicted by broken behavior.

The deletion problem drives the strongest choices: escalating confirmation friction (project delete = simple confirm dialog with a name chip; account delete = type-your-email confirm with a live <progress> matchbar in JetBrains Mono plus an 'I understand this is permanent.' checkbox), a numeric risk meter that differs between the two destructive actions (2/3 vs 3/3), and loss chips enumerating exactly what this account would lose.

Copy is tuned to the brief: the empty projects state reads 'Nothing to delete here.' and the post-deletion terminal state 'Account deleted / Nothing is left to manage here.' — neither would fit another brief's output.

The shell, however, is the standard SaaS settings template: Inter font, indigo #4338ca accent, white cards on a #f4f5f8 gray background, 212px sticky left sidebar, topbar with avatar initials — competent but interchangeable framing, which is what keeps this off a 5.

From the idle screenshot alone, before any source was read: purpose read immediately as account settings ('Account settings' header, sidebar Profile / Projects 3 / Danger zone, profile form, projects list with per-row trash icons, red Danger zone card) — matches the brief exactly.

Primary action read as 'Save changes' (filled purple, leftmost in the Profile footer, correctly muted while the form is clean); the two deletion surfaces demanded by the brief were both instantly locatable (trash icon per project row; Danger zone card for the account).

What needs attention read as the Danger zone card — red striped border, warning icon, full RISK meter, 'Permanent' badge — with the 'Setup pending' plan badge as secondary; both readings survived the brief check.
